I am an old man with no schooling, and my bones are too tired for new ways. In Shinyanga the rains come once and leave quickly, so my family has always planted the crops that do not ask for much—cassava and sorghum mixed together on this big land of ours. We cannot buy fertilizer or those expensive seeds from town; we keep our own seed and let the soil rest when it is tired. My sons and grandchildren will work the shamba with hoes as we always have, and when the weeds grow thick after the rains I will pay some young men from the village to help us for a few weeks.
